article.title: Data Drift Is Not the Same as Concept Drift
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: When a production model performs worse, teams often say that the data have drifted and retraining is needed. Drift, however, describes several different phenomena. Data drift usually means that the distribution of input features has changed. Customers may be older, transaction amounts may be higher because of inflation, or a channel may attract a different population. Label drift refers to a change in the distribution of the target, such as a default rate rising from two percent to four percent. Concept drift is more fundamental: the relationship between inputs and the target has changed. A feature that strongly predicted purchase last year may no longer have the same meaning today. These changes require different responses. Input drift does not automatically make a model wrong. A feature distribution can shift while the conditional relationship between features and outcome remains stable. The model may still rank customers well. Conversely, concept drift can damage performance even when marginal feature distributions look similar. Monitoring should therefore include several layers. Teams can track feature distributions, missingness, category frequencies, score distributions, calibration, ranking metrics, and outcome rates once labels arrive. They should compare changes with business events such as pricing updates, channel migrations, policy changes, or data-pipeline releases. Retraining should follow diagnosis rather than become an automatic reaction to any drift alert. If a pipeline bug changes a feature, retraining on corrupted data makes the problem worse. If inflation shifts transaction amounts, transforming or redefining the feature may be more appropriate. If customer behavior genuinely changes, new training data may help. Model monitoring also needs thresholds that reflect business risk. A small statistical difference can be detectable in a huge dataset without being operationally important. Alerts should therefore combine statistical distance with expected impact and persistence. The key question is not merely whether the data changed. It is whether the change affects the model’s ability to support the intended decision. Distinguishing data drift, label drift, and concept drift helps teams choose the right investigation instead of treating retraining as a universal repair button. Analysts should state the population, denominator, observation window, and decision rule before interpreting the result. A useful review separates the observed metric from the mechanism that produced it and from the action that should follow. This makes the conclusion easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文強調，指標本身不足以支撐決策。解讀百分比、彙總結果、model drift、非顯著結果或分類 threshold 時，都必須同時確認母體、分母、比較基準、統計不確定性以及實際 business cost。只有把觀察結果與資料生成機制、決策條件分開，才能避免過度解讀。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：percentage、集計値、model drift、非有意な結果、classification thresholdは、数値だけでは意思決定を支えられない。母集団、分母、比較基準、統計的不確実性、business costを確認し、観察結果とdata generating mechanism、decision ruleを分けて解釈する必要がある。
